abstract: Presents the front cover of the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Contents
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: policy regulatory and services; telecommunication network; radio communication; signal processing; applied electromagnetics; applied electronics; multimedia and software tool and applications.

articleTitle: Linked data approach to the PSI directive implementation: Supporting tools and lessons learned
abstract: This paper addresses the technical aspects and challenges of implementation of the revised European Directive on the Public Sector Information (2013/37/EU), emphasizing the role of Linked Data approach for improved interoperability and re-use. It points to several tools that have been developed at the Mihajlo Pupin Institute to support the implementation process i.e. the Serbian CKAN that can be used for cataloguing of open data, the RDF Data Cube Validation tool and the Exploratory Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Linked Data component for publishing and consuming of statistical data. The paper places a particular emphasis on the lessons learned and proposes recommendations for improving the interoperability of e-government services in Serbia.

articleTitle: Realisation of server application for acoustic sensors based on RTSP, RTP protocols
abstract: This paper presents realization of server for collecting and processing sound data from acoustic sensors based on RTSP and RTP protocols. Server has access to all sound data from all connected sensors, which makes it possible to apply more DSP audio algorithms on data. Sensors metadata and processing results are displayed using web server. By using internet browser user can monitor activities of sensors. The implementation is tested in two scenarios: communication in closed environment like in smart house, and communication over the Internet network. The presented example shows a good potential of the system for various acoustic sensing applications.

articleTitle: Real-time visualization of signals from electronic control units on mobile platforms
abstract: In this paper, we suggest method for implementation of system for real-time data display on devices such as smart phones and tablets, key distinction of which being multitude of operating systems and mutual incompatibility. Goal is to develop single multiplatform application which would consist of universal portable source code, which would allow for code to be compiled to match the target platform. This way, application will consistently keep it's functionalities on all supported platforms, without need for targeted modifications of source code to achieve compatibility with specifics of individual platform. This is achieved through use of C++ programming language, whose standardized compilers are available on almost all computer systems, accompanied by multiplatform Qt framework for implementation of user interaction.

articleTitle: One solution of the accurate summation using fixed-point accumulator
abstract: The accurate summation is algorithm for summing floating-point numbers with reduced rounding errors. This paper presents one solution of accurate summation problem using fixed- point accumulator. Implemented algorithm is compared with others and has performances and precision comparable with the best existing algorithms.

articleTitle: Organization design for network related managed services
abstract: Network related managed services represent a growing market in the Telecom industry; this paper explores the challenges of managing the managed services projects and proposes an organization design that would lead to a best value proposition.

articleTitle: Coherent radiation summation of two X-band nanosecond Gunn oscillators synchronized by a modulating pulse
abstract: In the paper, we compare total wave fields in the X-band for two reference coherent microwave sources and for two nanosecond Gunn oscillators with initial phase stabilization by a common modulating voltage pulse. It is shown that the wave fields agree well.

articleTitle: Full route energy cost metric
abstract: The Full route energy cost metric is intended for use in mobile ad hoc network (MANET) protocols. In the early stages of design of a routing algorithm for robotic orbital and on-planet systems, it is necessary to determine the computing algorithms of metrics. The proposed metric computing algorithm was developed as an attempt to replace statistical methods, based on ratio of the lost packets from neighbors, to the measurement methods of physical factors causing packet loss. The proposed metric also takes into the account transfer time with the signal power required for transmission on each route segment.

articleTitle: Analysing the effect of CCA duration in 802.15.4 networks with hidden nodes by using PRISM
abstract: An analysis of the effect of a nonstandard clear-channel assessment (CCA) interval in IEEE 802.15.4 nonbeacon-enabled networks consisting of nodes which send one packet to a sink and are partially hidden from the others is presented. By using the statistical model-checking capability of the PRISM model checker, we have obtained probabilities of successful sending and analysed the differences between the results for the standard and nonstandard CCA intervals.

Author Keywords: unslotted carrier sense multiple access with collision avoidance

articleTitle: Implementation of wireless control on electrical bridge cranes and gantry crane
abstract: The paper presents practical experiences during implementation of radio remote control to the electrical bridge cranes in machine room HEP "Perućica" and gantry crane at a lock on Tisa. In addition to the new way of control, also kept the old way of control from cabine cranes as provided with selector switch. Installation of radio remote control system compared to conventional wired controlling methods, significantly is improved the efficiency and safely handling cranes.

articleTitle: Novel selective CIC filter functions with improved magnitude response characteristics
abstract: Novel selective multiplerless Cascaded-Integrator-Comb (CIC) finite impulse response (FIR) filter functions with applications in modern communication systems are designed. The paper is focused on the analysis of the proposed CIC filters in comparison with existing classical CIC structures and some recent results reported in the literature. The simultaneous improvements in the passband and stopband of filter functions are achieved.

articleTitle: Xtext-based eclipse editor for linker configuration file
abstract: This paper presents implementation of the text editor for linker configuration files. The editor contains tools and options such as spell checker, autocomplete or syntax highlighting, etc. which facilitate development process. The solution contains a description of the syntax that should be used for writing configuration files which further determine the manner of interpretation and linking of object files. Xtext Eclipse framework has been used as development platform. Xtext provides very sophisticated, modern and practical API for describing and defining huge range of domain-specific languages. Syntax developed in Xtext is independent of Eclipse IDE and it can be used in any Java environment.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of European models for railway noise prediction
abstract: According to Directive 2002/49/EC relating to environmental noise assessment and management, all EU countries are obliged to make strategic noise maps for heavily populated areas. Some countries developed their own national method for noise prediction. In addition to road traffic, a railway traffic is, also, significant noise source in urban areas. This paper provides an overview of several models used in European countries for prediction of sound power of railway noise sources and attenuation due to sound propagation between noise source and receiver point.

articleTitle: Cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna for wireless applications
abstract: The paper presents a CDRA (Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna) designed for wireless military and commercial applications. The antenna has been designed to radiate at 6.7 GHz, with a 160 MHz bandwidth at −10 dB. The antenna is made from a dielectric material with high quality factor. The dielectric resonator is Ba1−xPbxNd2Ti5O14 (BNT) and its relative permittivity has a value of 85.2. The feed technique used is direct coupling to micro strip-line.

articleTitle: A DSP implementation of Bass Manager Module
abstract: This paper describes implementation of solution for DSP Bass Manager Module for Cirrus Logic digital signal processor. The course of implementation of this solution is divided into three phases. After implementation, module was tested and verified using bit-exact tests with set of 18 test vectors. This implementation fits into the limitations of the target platform regarding MIPS and memory usage and meets the requirements for execution in real time. Further improvement of this module would include an even higher level of optimization, in order to faster execution and spending less memory.

articleTitle: Dynamic channel assignment algorithms for supporting QoS based services in wireless cellular environments
abstract: The number of users employing multimedia services in cellular networks has been increased dramatically in the last decade. Multimedia services are more demanding compared to traditional voice services in terms of bandwidth availability and integrity. The capacity and the bandwidth reservation on demand according to QoS requirements are key concepts in mobile cellular communications. The available frequency spectrum is limited and the demand for enhanced mobile user facilities is increasing day by day, hence the channels must be reused as much as possible to increase the system capacity. Existing and proposed channel assignment strategies have to be transformed to support efficiently the new demanding multimedia services. Through this paper we present a review of the most known channel assignment strategies, as well as their QoS aspects and we propose new DCA variations and a channel architecture adapted to QoS requirements for supporting multimedia services. We also present some strategies, models and conclusions for algorithm evaluation based on experimental results.

articleTitle: Automation testing of Bootloader for target DSP platform
abstract: In this paper is given the implementation of solutions for automated testing of Bootloader on the target DSP platform. Existing tools for manual testing do not meet the challenges of developing modern products, and its necessity for higher percentages of automation. The aim is to save time testing, reducing the occurrence of errors during testing due to human factors, and the ability that testing may execute a person who has no previous knowledge of a given field.

articleTitle: Analysis of TLM air-vent model applicability to EMC problems
abstract: In this paper, a numerical analysis of the shielding properties related to a protective metal enclosure with ventilation apertures is performed. As a numerical tool, the TLM method, either in conventional form based on fine mesh to describe apertures presence or enhanced with the compact air-vent model is used. The main focus in the paper is on examining the limits of applying the compact air-vent model for EMC problems solving.

articleTitle: Linearization of microstrip RF power amplifier loaded with the broadband matching circuits for the efficiency maintenance
abstract: In this paper a RF amplifier is designed in microstrip technique for broadband application in the frequency range 0.75-1.15 GHz. Its linearization has been performed by the second- and fourth-order nonlinear signals fed at the transistor gate and drain throughout the broadband matching circuits designed to provide high amplifier efficiency and adequate power level of the injected linearization signals. The effects of the linearization are considered through the simulation for two sinusoidal signals with different frequency interval between them setting on from 10 MHz and going up to 50 MHz at different input power levels up to saturation, as well as for an OFDM digitally modulated signal.

Author Keywords: second- and fourth-order nonlinear signals and intermodulation products

articleTitle: Enhancing use case point estimation method using fuzzy algorithms
abstract: This paper comes out due to importance of software project effort estimation in software engineering. Effort estimation depends on functionality, productivity, number of transactions etc. This paper tends to check out if productivity appraisal (by using fuzzy logic) is able to improve the effort estimation. Exposed results show substantial statistical (percentage) enhancement when using the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Device for measuring one-way network delay with microsecond accuracy
abstract: A comprehensive assessment of Internet connection quality requires detailed knowledge of IP performance metrics. This article focuses on the creation of a hardware and software complex entitled NetTestBox, which is able to measure one-way delay and available bandwidth between remote nodes. The measuring technology uses time synchronization via GPS/GLONASS receivers. The principles of operation of the specially written owping software used for measuring one-way delay with microsecond accuracy are discussed in detail, with the results of the first tests on real networks also shown.

articleTitle: LTE performance in a hybrid indoor DAS (Active vs. Passive)
abstract: This paper analyses LTE performance of active and passive sections in a medium-size hybrid Distributed Antenna System (DAS), in real indoor conditions. Overall, the measurements have shown similar results at both sections, in terms of latency and throughput. The passive portion outperforms the active in average FTP DL throughput by 7.3%, while FTP UL throughputs are nearly the same, differing by less than 0.3%. The results indicate that the utilization of expensive active elements in small to medium-size In-Building Solutions (IBS) is reasonable for overcoming large cable lengths, but does not necessarily imply better LTE performance.

articleTitle: One software solution for processing WebVTT subtitles during playback of hls streams using FFmpeg libraries
abstract: Paper presents one implementation of software solution for processing WebVTT subtitles during playback of HLS streams. Software solution is created by using the functionality of the FFmpeg library. Result of using created software solution on HLS streams is creation of overall transport stream, which contains video, audio and subtitle components. In this way successful playback of audio, video and subtitle is enabled.

articleTitle: Effect of phase noise on error performance of DE-QPSK receiver over k-μ fading channel
abstract: This paper presents the error performance analysis of differentially encoded coherent quadrature phase-shift keying (DE-QPSK) transmission over k-μ fading channel. The imperfections of the carrier signal recovery are taken into consideration through the phase-locked loop error, which is described by Tikhonov distribution. Based on novel derived expression for average bit-error probability (BEP), numerical results are obtained. The influence of loop's bandwidth-bit time product and fading depth on the system performance is investigated.

articleTitle: Compact device for detecting single event effects in semiconductor components
abstract: The paper describes a compact system for detecting Single Event Effects (SEE) in semiconductor components. The SEE is caused by a hit into a electronic chip with an energetic particle. The hit can cause unexpected behaviour of the system. The tested component is called Device Under Test (DUT). The structure of the system is shown and used components are described with their main tasks. Some of results of the running system are shown.

articleTitle: Android application as parental control service in car
abstract: This paper explains Android service for sending and receiving e-mail in case speeding has occurred. Client app has been made for changing e-mail sender, receiver and also for changing speed limits for particular section of road. Evaluation has shown that fetching data from service is quite reliable and safe. This is because OBD II system is used only for reading data and not for writing them on CAN bus.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable multi-robot virtual environment
abstract: This paper presents the development and the use of reconfigurable virtual robot laboratory for programming, simulation and control of multi-robot operation. Special attention is devoted to fulfillment of basic requirements of the reconfigurability: modularity, scalability, and openness. The reconfigurability of the virtual environment can be considered from two aspects: as a possibility of reconfiguring operational mode and as a possibility of reconfiguring virtual robots and virtual environment. The developed environment is applied in robot programming, testing and remote control to demonstrate its effectiveness. It represents an integrated solution for control of multiple robots with continuous adjustment to the real laboratory environment and robots' usage.

articleTitle: Verification of train localization by using inertial measurement system and identification of characteristic segments
abstract: In this paper, the possibility of using an accelerometer-gyroscope based inertial sensor to improve a train locating system based on satellite navigation is described. Disadvantages of the inertial sensors are introduced as well as the calculation of desired data and their filtration. A poly-phase filter design is described as a possible solution for distortion elimination. A design approach of a prototype device which implements the inertial measurement and filtration is also described. The device is equipped with four sensors and it is connectable with a common PC by using USB. The software interface is suited for usage with LabVIEW software.

articleTitle: GPU-based implementation of reverb effect
abstract: Graphics processing units (GPUs) have been increasingly used in different engineering applications in the past several years. One of the main application areas is digital signal processing, especially in the domain of audio, image, and video processing. Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) is often core part of those processing algorithms, and it is efficiently implemented on the GPUs through available libraries. In this paper, we focus on audio signal processing, and present an implementation of convolution reverb effect on the NVIDIA GPUs using CUDA. Implemented effect is tested with carefully chosen set of examples and we observed significant speedups over reference, CPU implementation. Finally, the results are briefly discussed with emphasize on benefits and drawbacks of using GPUs in such application.

articleTitle: Enabling high performance cloud computing using zero touch provisioning
abstract: For over a decade, the data requirements of e-Science applications increase drastically with the emergence of data-intensive applications. The efficient usage of these complex applications that involve the composition of services horizontally, but also vertically across multiple networks, demand a guaranteed level of quality of service to be provided. At the same time user requirements remain strict on not overburdening users with too many configuration tasks and deep knowledge of the underlying components. Aiming to provide the means to employ multiple cloud services for collaborative e-Science project in this paper we explore the possibilities of the zero touch provisioning concepts used on top of a dedicated on-demand establishment of direct customer-provider routes within the European Research and Educational Network - GEANT.

articleTitle: Call-delay investigation in a client-content server environment
abstract: The present paper is a continuation work investigating more in depth the issue of important client call delay in a client-server communication environment, triggered by a server overload condition. The problem has been detected by the authors during a test-phase related to experiments performed for a research project dedicated to content delivery over IP networks.

articleTitle: Software support of the process of managing intellectual property
abstract: This paper discusses the software support of the process of managing intellectual property in the SME company whose core business is software development for digital television, smart homes, set-top boxes and automotive industries as well as research projects in digital television and multimedia systems. Mentioned software support includes a system for the management of patents as a primary form of intellectual property. The system includes client-server architecture, whereby client side includes interface applications that can represent a standard Web browser (eg. Firefox), and server side includes a web server. The ongoing implementation of the system is organized including KnowledgeTree client/server platform. This system software support includes modules which are needed for the patenting process and they are available over the internet.

articleTitle: Performance of high efficiency video coding (HEVC) HM-16.6 encoder
abstract: This paper seeks to provide performance analysis for High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) HM-16.6 reference coder for different resolution test sequences and picture structures. The HEVC coder is tested for the fixed Quantization Parameter (QP) value in lowdelay configurations, when Main profile with P and hierarchical B pictures, respectively, is used. Simulation results have shown differences in bit-rate and encoding time saving, as well as small difference in SNR values for luma component of picture. Beside objective results, subjective video assessments for all tested sequences are presented, too.

articleTitle: Automated testing of electronic control units in a hardware-in-the-loop simulation environment
abstract: The electronic control units (ECU) are used in modern products/devices to add new and automate existing functions. The development of such products usually requires the involvement of a several teams that will work on smaller parts of project (components or subsystems). Each of the participants in the development process performs independent testing of their part of project, but also it is necessary to integrate all these components/subsystems into the final product and test together their performance as a whole. This paper presents a solution for automated diagnostics of electronic control units, primarily with a goal of saving time and resources, as well as increasing security. Also, described environment is used for tracking progress, generating reports, and synchronization of activities.

articleTitle: Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients as features for automatic speaker recognition
abstract: Automatic speaker recognizer can be based on the use of mel-frequency cepstral coefficients as speaker features. Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients depend on energy inside considered auditory critical bands. These auditory critical bands model masking phenomena. Application of triangular auditory critical bands results in better recognition accuracy with respect to the case when rectangular auditory critical bands are applied. Recognition accuracy when exponential auditory critical bands are applied outperforms recognition accuracy of automatic speaker recognizer when triangular or rectangular auditory critical bands are applied. Application of transformation on elements of speaker model, which target decreasing of difference between testing and training models of the same speaker, can increase recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: IP cores for 2D direct and inverse discrete cosine transformation
abstract: IP cores for direct and inverse discrete cosine transformation are important part of compression core implementation. In this paper the results for the implementation of two dimensional binary discrete cosine transformation (2D binDCT) and two dimensional binary discrete cosine inverse transformation (2D binIDCT) algorithm which are discrete cosine transformation/ discrete cosine inverse transformation (DCT/IDCT) approximations are presented. Besides, binDCT and binlDCT algorithm acceleration gain compared to the software implementation is given. It is shown that hardware implementation is 3 to 100 times faster compared to software implementation.

articleTitle: Enhancing local economic development using collective intelligence
abstract: This paper focus on collecting opinions and suggestions by entrepreneurs in order to enhance local economic development. Questions are expressed in the form of crowdsourcing pool, and answers are clustered by similarity. The frequency of similar answers obtained by the same or similar questions may point to obstacles for economic development that local government institutions should solve.

articleTitle: Recent advances in location prediction methods for cellular communication networks
abstract: Predicting the future location of a device inside a cellular network has become an interesting field of study in recent years, as it offers new solutions for location based services. In this paper we analyze recently proposed methods for location prediction. Based on the proven limits of human predictability we propose that location prediction methods should not be limited only to movement pattern analysis. We conclude that location prediction methods can become more accurate by introducing social analysis methods based on call related information obtained from the network or the user's device.

articleTitle: Performances of random codes based on Quasigroups for transmission of audio files
abstract: Error-correcting codes can be applied for transmission of images and audio files through a noise channel. Application of Random Codes Based on Quasigroups (RCBQ) for image transmission is considered elsewhere. In this paper we investigate performances of these codes for transmission of audio files through a binary-symmetric channel. We present and analyze several experimental results obtained using Cut-Decoding and 4-Sets-Cut-Decoding algorithms defined for RCBQ. In the experiments we use code (72, 576) with rate 1/8. We made experiments with Beethovens "Ode to Joy".

articleTitle: Coplanar waveguide to microstrip transition in thin polymer film for characterization and packaging of microwave photonic components
abstract: We report in this paper two types of broadband transitions between microstrip and coplanar lines on thin benzocyclobutene (BCB) polymer substrate. They are both via-free, using electromagnetic coupling between the bottom and top ground planes, which simplifies the manufacturing of components driven by microstrip electrodes. In the first ones, the bottom ground is not patterned, which makes them particularly suitable to on-wafer measurement of components under development with coplanar probes. An ultra-broad bandwidth of 68 GHz (from 1 GHz to 69 GHz) was achieved with 20-pm BCB. In the second ones, intended for connectorizing components on thin substrate with coplanar connectors, the bottom ground is patterned to match the narrow center conductor (54 μm) on thin substrate to the wide center conductor (127 μm) of the connector with a tapered section, achieving to a experimental bandwidth 13 GHz for the moment.

articleTitle: Evaluation of load balancing in HSUPA
abstract: The paper considers a problem of load balancing, i.e. allocation of single-carrier User Equipment (UE) entities over multiple available carriers in the Wideband Code Division Multiple Access (W-CDMA) High Speed Uplink Packet Access (HSUPA) system. Performance of different load balancing approaches is numerically evaluated by means of System Level Simulations (SLS) of W-CDMA HSUPA. The simulation results demonstrate a sufficient performance gain due to optimal carrier selection at the beginning of a packet call compared to random carrier selection at the beginning of a call. An additional minor gain is achievable for high traffic loads if optimal carrier reassignment is allowed also during the packet calls. The gains in both cases are explained by better equalization of physical resources assigned to different UEs and by suppression of the intra-cell interference at the most loaded carriers.

articleTitle: The concept of remote tuner in digital television software
abstract: Tuners are physical devices that allow television systems to lock to the desired frequency and receive the modulated television signal. The appearance of Internet television has enabled the development of remotely controlled virtual tuners. That concept has provided grounds for the realization of more flexible television distribution architectures. In the paper, the concept is analyzed and emerging technology (SAT>IP) that makes use of the concept is presented. The overhead introduced with the use of remote tuner is estimated for the case of two typical operations: channel zapping and frequency scanning. In the case of channel zapping, the overhead can be neglected.

articleTitle: PVR trick-mode emulation through consecutive jumps
abstract: This paper presents a possible way of emulating PVR trick-modes on a DTV set top box through consecutive jumps. The solution is interesting for set top boxes without hardware decoder trick-mode support. Essential part of trick-mode emulation through consecutive jumps is I-frame analysis that takes place during PVR recording phase. Another important aspect of solution is its adaptive format, where additional analyses are carried out in order to establish time realistic navigation through file, regardless of system workload.

articleTitle: Detection of the external magnetic field polarity through the inductance voltage harmonic phase order
abstract: Inductance is a basic electrical element that couples magnetic flux and current. In many applications the linear approximation of inductance provides sufficiently good results of analysis. In the presence of an additional DC bias magnetic field HDC, the observed B-H curve is forced to be moved from its unbiased state and an asymmetric nonlinearity of the targeted inductance is produced. Diagnostic method is proposed, which couples voltage harmonic phases and the direction of HDC bias field by means of the LT Spice simulation. An experimental verification of the proposed technique is successfully accomplished, along with the settlement of the further research.

articleTitle: UWB wireless system for falling down detection
abstract: The paper contains a description of the wireless solution intended for falling down detection. The detection functions are embedded into UWB positioning system. The paper describes general system architecture and presents falling down detection algorithm. The results of experiments performed during algorithm development phase as well as tests of the system and detection algorithm are also included.

articleTitle: Stablo uređaja u jezgru Linuksa i podrška za emulator QeMU i OS Android
abstract: Jezgro Linuksa je projekat koji se neprestano usavršava u skladu sa potrebama korisnika i trendovima u dizajnu i implementaciji operativnih sistema. U tom svetlu, jedna od funkcionalnosti jezgra Linuksa koja privlaci dosta pažnje u poslednje vreme jeste podrška za stablo uredaja. Sa druge strane, iako je OS Android zasnovan na jezgru Linuksa, on nije, donedavno, uopšte koristio funkcionalnosti jezgra vezana za stablo uređaja. U ovom radu je opisano kako je implementirana podrška za stablo uredaja u emulatoru Androida za platformu MIPS.

articleTitle: One solution for rendering translucent 2D UI elements in 3D space
abstract: This paper describes a rendering system designed to render translucent 2D UI elements (e.g. images and text) in 3D space. Significant part of the implemented system and algorithm is dedicated to rendering of composite 2D elements consisting of multiple simple elements in the same plane in 3D space. The described approach was incorporated in a UI development framework which is used by several real world applications developed for consumer electronics devices.

articleTitle: Teleoperation system control based on the method for supervisory control with variable time delay
abstract: Teleoperation is the technique of controlling a system from a remote location, which consists of a master and a slave system. The master system usually represents the model of the slave system controlled by an operator. The slave system is usually dislocated in relation to the master system and is controlled by commands sent from the master system over a communication channel. The concept of Supervisory management is generally used up to indicate that one or more human operators set the initial conditions for the control, monitoring and alternately adjusting and receiving information from the computer that is closing the control loop by itself, via external sensors. The mobile robot performs certain tasks using IR sensors, the operator monitors his work and makes some changes in the way the mobile robot works, if necessary.

articleTitle: Survey of Android security model enhancement to meet the conditional access system requirements in digital video broadcasting systems
abstract: This paper discusses Android security model and ways of enchasing it to meet the Conditional Access Systems requirements in Digital Video Broadcasting. Security enchantments involve usage of virtualization methods to separate CA and user systems in order to reduce its attack surface.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of texture classification based on low and high order local features
abstract: The importance of texture for recognition of objects, scenes and events is well-known and used in various computer vision tasks. Until recently, best-performing texture classification algorithms relied on processing of low-level local features and statistical learning based adjustment of classifiers. Convolutional neural networks introduced higher order local features and improved classification results significantly. In this paper, we compared texture classification based on low-lever and high order local features. Also, we demonstrated the ability of convolutional networks to learn high order features from one dataset and to efficiently use that knowledge on a different dataset.

articleTitle: LDPC (512,480) genetic design as alternative to CRC in implementation of AODV routing protocol stack
abstract: This paper presents a design of LDPC (Low Density Parity Check) code. Algorithm deals with code optimization based on Tanner graph mutations. The LDPC code was designed to replace CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check) code in the application of a tiny AODV routing protocol stack. Own AODV routing protocol stack was previously designed especially for wireless sensor networks with constrained resources and it is intended for usage in wireless mesh network formed by Intelligent firemen suits. Link layer of target platform uses 64B long packet with 4B for LDPC parity. The code was designed to provide the most optimal detection and correction capability with the lowest possible parity bites.

articleTitle: The extrapolation of failure rate of electrical components in specific operational conditions
abstract: This paper deals with a method for estimating the reliability of the electronic components, that are used in the design of electronic devices within complex systems. Mentioned methods provide a common base for comparison and evaluation of the design reliability and represent a tool that allows increasing the reliability of the proposed device. This article discusses a stress models, derived from the international standard ČSN EN 61709 ed.2 and reliability prediction handbook MIL-HDBK-217, which allows estimation of the effect changes in the environmental conditions on component reliability.

articleTitle: Fast-deployment and continuous monitoring through REM: A low-cost device prototype
abstract: This work addresses the issue of coexistence among different technologies into the 2.4 GHz Industrial Scientific and Medical (ISM) band. A low-cost device is prototyped in order to derive multi-standard Radio Environmental Maps (REM) useful for fast deployment of technologies in environments affected by interference. In particular, the device creates coverage maps, allowing to identify the best channel to be used by a given technology. Some examples of experimental results are presented to demonstrate the utility of the developed prototype.

articleTitle: Video watermark detection in DCT domain for H.264/AVC through a hierarchical prior
abstract: With the advance of digital communications the distribution of video content has become common place. In this framework digital video watermarking can be a promising solution in a digital rights management system. H.264/AVC is a state of the art video coding standard and has been used in many applications. In this work, we propose a two-level hierarchical prior in the framework of intra-coded DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform) coefficients in H.264/AVC video stream. It is well known that Gaussian, Laplacian, Generalized Gaussian distribution (GGD) and Cauchy distributions exhibit improved capabilities for the description of the empirical DCT coefficients. For the bipolar additive watermark in H.264/AVC video stream, the aforementioned distributions have been proved a base for improved detection algorithms. In this framework, the proposed watermark detection based on the hierarchical prior, deserves further investigation. Thus our simulation results show improved detection performance along with improved robustness against different attacks.

articleTitle: Compressed sensing MRI using nonseparable shearlet transform and split Bregman algorithm
abstract: We analyze the use of discrete nonseparable shearlet transform for sparse representation of the MRI image. This transform is a non-tight frame, but has excellent localization properties in the spatial domain. Additionally, we exploit the frequency representation of the canonical dual filters of this transform and combine it with the measurement process, carried out in the Fourier domain, to implement the split Bregman algorithm for reconstruction. We compare the performance of the proposed approach to approaches using split Bregman algorithm with curvelets, wavelets and total variation.

articleTitle: Network topology exchange between NetFPGA-10G and Quagga routing platforms
abstract: Internet is getting faster and more dynamic daily, with increasing number of users, and mobility on the network. This puts a high load on Internet routers, which are the most important component of the Internet infrastructure. In this paper, we present and analyze integration of Quagga open-source routing software and NetFPGA-10G hardware platform. These two open-source platforms allow us to evaluate speed of connection between control and data planes which is crucial for flexibility of Internet routers and their potential to follow fast changes on the Internet. In particular, we measure how fast lookup tables calculated by the control plane can be downloaded to hardware in order to allow high-speed packet forwarding using balanced parallelized frugal lookup (BPFL) algorithm, which we proposed earlier. BPFL achieves high speed in packet forwarding using parallel processing on FPGA chip. Further, BPFL uses less on-chip memory compared to other lookup algorithms, and, for this reason, it can more scalable support IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

articleTitle: Ultra low power capcitive touch sensor
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to examine how good is given solution for low power consumption controllers by Atmel. As addition measurements for CPU load, current consumption and response time for controller ATSAMD20, coupled with low power sensor QT2, were conducted. Results of measurements were compared with results given by manufacturer. Principles of operation and design of low power sensors are explained in text.

articleTitle: Distributed MIMO techniques in wireless sensor networks with relays
abstract: In this paper we propose new solution for improving performance of the wireless sensor networks with relay stations, through distributed Multiple Input-Multiple Output implementation, i.e. by creating virtual Orthogonal Space Time Block Coding systems. The considered scheme provides creating virtual 2×1 Multiple Input-Single Output channel. This system besides sensor nodes includes one base station, and one relay station equipped with two antennas, or two relay stations each equipped with a single antenna. The simulation results show that the proposed solution can provide evidently better Bit Error Rate performance.

articleTitle: A multi-objective assessment framework for cloud computing
abstract: In this paper we propose a multi-objective assessment framework for cloud computing technology. Starting from the technology itself, we perform top down approach, decomposing primary objectives: economy, ecology, business and social, into hierarchical structure. Decomposition is performed until the level at which quantification of objectives is possible and appropriate decision space appears recognizable. To fit the scope of this paper, we provide only representative parts of the framework.

articleTitle: Analysis of system with pure time-delay using computer algebra systems
abstract: In this paper, a new approach of solving the continuous-time systems, with pure time-delay elements, using symbolic tools is presented. Although symbolic computer tools cannot find the closed form solution in frequency domain (using Laplace transform method), the final solution can be derived in time domain. Described symbolic solution is implemented by using software package Mathematica (the Wolfram language), and application package SchematicSolver.

articleTitle: Robust hermite transform based on the L-estimate principle
abstract: Hermite transform has been used In various signal processing applications due to many desirable properties. Particularly, when compared with the trigonometric functions, Hermite functions provide better computational localization in both signal and transform domains. Therefore, this transform has been applied in image compression, tomography, biomedical applications, etc. However, the performance of the Hermite transform may be degraded in the presence of impulse noise, which appears in real applications, for instance, during signal transmission. In such cases, an L-estimation approach is used to mitigate the noise effect. In this paper, the L-estimation approach is applied to the Hermite transform. The goal is to improve signal processing results in the cases of noisy signals for which Hermite transform gives suitable representation. The proposed solution is tested under pure impulse and under combination of the impulse and Gaussian noise, showing improved results in both cases.

articleTitle: Psychoacoustic analysis of decimation filter parameters influence on the quality of audio signals
abstract: Downsampling is a widely spread procedure in audio signal processing. This paper considers the influence of decimation filters on the resulting audio signal. Decimation filters role is suppression of all spectral components higher than one half of the new sampling frequency in order to avoid aliasing. Demands for stopband attenuation of these filters are usually very rigorous. This paper investigates how justified are there requests from psychoacoustic point of view. Basic procedure in such a research is subjective testing. Aside from objective measures, subjective evaluation is one of the key parameters that can describe the characteristics of given audio signal processing. The results of testing different filters on perceptibility of aliased components are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Efficient adaptation and high reusability of test suites in a black box testing environment
abstract: In rapid software development environments, as software component reusability can provide significant win in productivity, the test plan readiness became essential for project success. In these conditions, when a large test plans (with high number of test cases) have to be ready and available in short time, the reusability of test cases that were already developed for specific software component is necessary.

articleTitle: Quality measurements of an UWB reduced-size CPW-fed aperture antenna
abstract: The paper presents a characterization of a compact co-planar waveguide (CPW)-fed slot loaded low return loss planar printed antenna designed for wireless communication and ultra-wideband (UWB) applications. Following a review of the antenna design, which was implemented and simulated using Agilent's Advanced Design System (ADS), the paper presents laboratory measurements of relative gain and impulse response transformed from the frequency domain. An antenna quality metric based on time-domain S21 is discussed and related to antenna quality metrics such as the System Fidelity Factor (SFF).

articleTitle: Advanced numerical solution algorithms for modern EM wave propagation problems
abstract: The development of high-order, finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) schemes for modeling and investigating radio-wave propagation problems are presented in this work. The electromagnetic waves can be reproduced precisely in a well-defined discretized space of any geometry, giving accurate simulation results with reasonable computational resources. Special consideration is given to the correct boundary conditions enforced at the media interfaces, as well as to the absorbing boundary conditions that terminate the FDTD grid in open-region problems.

articleTitle: Outage analysis in clustered cooperative networks over K fading channels
abstract: In this paper, the outage probability of a clustered cooperative decode-and-forward wireless networks is investigated, subject to Rayleigh fading and Gamma shadowing. Outage probability expression is derived when the fusion centre selects the stronger received transmission out of the maximal ratio combined relayed packets and (if any) repeated packets from the originating node. The effects of average signal-to-noise ratio values, network dimension, packet length as well as shadowing spread is discussed.

articleTitle: Automation of Nordig verification for digital TV receivers
abstract: This paper describes process of automation of the Nordig test suite and presents savings in time that have been achieved by automating part of the test suite.

articleTitle: Microwave bandpass filter with quasi-lumped elements
abstract: In this paper, a new approach for microwave bandpass filters design is presented using quasi-lumped elements. The resonator is realized as a double-sided microstrip structure with two quasi-lumped elements: a square spiral inductor and a patch capacitor each printed on separate layer. Using this resonator, three bandpass filters with different types of feeder realization are designed. Furthermore, electric-circuit models are proposed instead of the three-dimensional electromagnetic (3D EM) models, which are suitable for microwave filters design. This approach is used to finally design a triple-bandpass filter.

articleTitle: Software module for registering provided health services and consumed medications in infirmary
abstract: In this paper, the software module for recording health services provided and consumed medications in the infirmary is shown. The presented software module provides software support for medical staff in the hospital, enabling the billing of health services provided to patients who are hospitalized in infirmary at the health center. Also, the software module allows monitoring and recording of consumed drugs and medical supplies (medicaments), generating e-invoices, as well as generating a larger number of fixed reports. The presented module can function as a standalone desktop application or in conjunction with medical information system (MIS) MEDIS.NET. In addition to possible horizontal integration with MIS MEDIS.NET and system for dynamically generating reports there is vertical integration with RFZO unit via electronic invoices, by checking patients insurance and loading codebooks for secondary care provided by RFZO. Presented software module currently is in used in several health care institutions and it is in closely associated with the MIS MEDIS.NET.

articleTitle: Parameters of efficiency of contact center
abstract: The paper deals with measurable parameters of efficiency of contact centers and their mutual influence. The analysis is based on results obtained using the comparative method of published studies of foreign contact centers. Two key indicators of effective work of the contact center as retaining existing and attracting new users, which directly affects the overall success of the company.

articleTitle: A stochastic whitening algorithm with time variable neuron slope for blind DFE
abstract: The self-optimized blind decision feedback equalizer (DFE), which independently optimizes feed-forward and feedback filters, deals with the feedback filter mismatch. To mitigate the filter mismatch effects, we have proposed a stochastic entropy gradient algorithm with a time variable neuron slope for all-pole filter which acts as a front-end amplitude equalizer in the blind operation mode. The algorithm performances are verified by simulations for 16- and 64-QAM (quadrature amplitude modulated) signals.

articleTitle: Comparing human and automated speaker recognition in case of imitated speech
abstract: The voice of each speaker is unique, which means that speaker identification based on voice is possible, but there are no reliable methods for that, yet. The reason is that the voice of a speaker can vary a lot and that different voices can sometimes sound quite similar. The aim of this research is to determine which features are the most important to humans for speaker identification, as well as features which the automated speaker recognition system relies on.

articleTitle: On the cryptographic system vulnerabilities
abstract: In this article, influence of the generation and usage of cryptographic keys, message formatting and way of system implementation to the security of protected messages are analyzed. Quoted practical examples we showed that application of each of those actions in improper way, even used with cryptographically good ciphering algorithm, might lead to insecure system.

articleTitle: One solution for remote calibration and measurement of electronic control units
abstract: This paper introduces one solution for remote calibration and measurement of modern automobile Electronic Control Unit. Proposed solution is based on HyperText Transfer Protocol and Universal Measurement and Calibration Protocol on Ethernet computer network. Introduction of embedded computer and wireless network enables portable solution for remote calibration and measurement of Electronic Control Units.

articleTitle: Analysis of the results obtained by intelligent method for project portfolio scheduling
abstract: A key factor at the project portfolio scheduling is about aiming at a pool of projects due the multi-objective environment in which modern organizations operate. Recent works proposed multi-objective models that are close to real world projects and they are based on intelligent methods. This work is an evaluation of this approach. More specifically, selected research questions are statistically tested, while some of them have been answered positively, proving the performance of the overall solving method.

articleTitle: Optimization of H.264 video decoder from Android OS for MIPS32 DSP ASE architectures
abstract: The aim of this study is to present the steps of optimization the H.264 / AVC video decoder for MIPS32 DSP ASE SIMD (Single-instruction, multiple-data) processor architecture. In particular, SIMD architecture can be very efficient in the implementation of video applications which have simple operations on 8-bit or 16-bit samples. Besides already mentioned architecture it is also important to get familiar with the H.264 / AVC video code standards. The parts of decoder that were subject of optimization were detected as the biggest consumers of CPU resources. After optimization, overall system speedup gain was 36%.

articleTitle: A relational database role in handling fuzziness of real world
abstract: In this paper we deal with relevance and possibilities of fuzzy relational databases regarding its applications in data managing and manipulation. Authors have presented contributions, aspects and approaches in solving different tasks in relational databases using fuzzy concept. Fuzzy logic and fuzzy relations play a crucial role in overcoming the limitations of traditional relational databases including data representation, date retrieval, knowledge discovery, data classification, data mining, approximate reasoning, and other data intensive applications. Actually, we cannot neglect facts that data and rules expressing real world are not always crisp. This paper presents perspectives of fuzzy relational databases in attempts to apply these concepts into the practice and methods for handling with fuzzy data.

articleTitle: Hybrid set top box system that combines DVB input with the data from internet server
abstract: This paper represents a system which combines two different types of contents on hybrid set top box (STB) device: DVB data and data from Internet server. Hybrid STB is based on Android operating system and it is equipped with support for playback of DVB and IP (using HLS protocol) services. For services received from DVB data flow, EPG data is replaced with EPG data from the Internet server.

Author Keywords: uređaj za prijem digitalnog signala (STB uređaj)

articleTitle: Non-regenerative cooperative relaying in precise agriculture communication platform
abstract: Precision agriculture is a farm management system with the goal of optimizing resources for the improved crop production. Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are recognized as an important tool in gathering information necessary for decision making system. However, energy consumption is considered as one of the most important issues in their implementation, since the lifetime of the network is limited with the battery-powered sensor nodes. In that manner, different techniques for energy savings under different wireless channel conditions are explored. One of the promising techniques to improve wireless system performance with the reduced transmit power is cooperative relaying. Therefore, in this paper we present performance analyses of two hop amplify-and-forward cooperative relay system when implemented in WSNs. The analyzed communication system is applicable to various fading scenarios characterized with different Ricean K factors and average signal to noise ratios (SNR). It has been shown that adequate positioning of the relay nodes in the network along with the nodes' cooperation leads to considerable energy savings in the considered WSNs.

articleTitle: MIMO antenna selection analysis based on QoS and antenna correlation indicator statistics
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna selection is investigated by the means of system statistical parameters to determine patterns to minimize co-channel interference into orthogonal frequency division multiplexing access (OFDM) based network. Analytical method to predict LTE MIMO data throughput at different AoA and antenna configurations is given and illustrated by LTE based experiments in the indoor lab environment at 1800 MHz frequency band.

articleTitle: Fractal dimension of time-activity curves in dynamic parathyroid scintigraphy
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present a method for distinguishing the parathyroid tumor from the surrounding tissue based on fractal dimension of time-activity curves obtained in the dynamic phase of conventional double-tracer protocol (dynamic sestamibi parathyroid scintigraphy). The application of this method is illustrated through three examples of histopathologically proven parathyroid tumors and the results are compared with results of subtraction and Submarine interpretation.

articleTitle: A bioinformatic system for collecting and processing environmental data
abstract: The paper presents a system for collecting, transferring and processing environmental data, implemented within the Centre of Excellence in Bioinformatics (BIO-ICT). Environmental data, collected by three weather stations, are transferred to a remote server via a specially designed and developed GPRS communication device. At the server side, the received data are stored into a database and further processed. The proposed system is scalable in a sense that it provides very simple inclusion of additional weather stations. The system envisions the use of collected data in a decision-making process supported by a model specially developed for the corresponding climate and weather conditions.

articleTitle: Self-sufficient system for NOx reduction
abstract: This paper describes a SCR system which is being developed for using with the diesel engines. Unlike the commercial products this system has not to be connected with the electrical control units or sensors of the target engine. It means the system is not dependent on the vehicle type. The goal of this project is to develop a self-sufficient system for the reduction of nitrogen oxides. This feature enables using the same system in wide range of projects, including retrofitting. It also describes whole hardware principle and the interconnection between modules. Additionally the basic behavior of the catalytic convertor is described and demonstrated by the results of several tests on the test bench.

articleTitle: Interference estimation in wireless mobile random waypoint networks
abstract: It is well known that the stochastic nature of the interference deeply impacts on the performance of emerging and future wireless communication systems. In this work we consider an ad hoc network where the nodes move according to the Random Waypoint mobility model. Assuming a time-varying wireless channel due to slow and fast fading and, considering the dynamic path loss due to the mobility of the nodes, we start by characterizing the interference distribution caused to a receiver by the moving interferers located in a ring. Based on the interference distribution, we evaluate two different methodologies to estimate the interference in real-time. The accuracy of the results achieved with the proposed methodologies in several simulations show that they may used as an effective tool of interference estimation in future wireless communication systems, being the main contribution of this work.

articleTitle: Automatic detection of different mechanical ERDPF configurations
abstract: The Electrically Regenerable Diesel Particulate Filter is primary intended as part of an exhaust system which is able to use for a vehicle retrofitting. The portfolio of target applications is wide therefore it was necessary to design an electronic system which will be usable for all hardware configurations of ERDPF filters without any changes in firmware of the electronic control system. The electronic system was designed as a modular system which uses the new automatic detection methodology of mechanical ERDPF constructions. The automatic detection function is based on the bus switches and measuring of power consumption.

articleTitle: The algorithm for automatic segmentation of breast and pectoral muscle regions from mammograms
abstract: Proper segmentation of breast and pectoral muscle regions is often the first step in systems for automatic analysis of mammographic images. This paper proposes a method for extraction of the breast region using adaptive gamma correction algorithm for image contrast enhancement and k-means algorithm for thresholding the image in order to extract background and the breast region. To extract the pectoral muscle we find the region of interest, enhance its contrast, and find the region of muscle using k-means algorithm. To estimate the curve representing the edge of the pectoral muscle we use cubic polynomial fitting. The efficiency of the proposed method is tested on mammograms from miniMIAS database.

articleTitle: Programska implementacija sistema za prikupljanje i obradu signala sa elektronskih kontrolnih jedinica u automobilskoj mreži
abstract: Savremeni automobili mogu imati više desetina elektronskih kontrolnih jedinica (EKJ) koje izmedu sebe razmenjuju više stotina pa čak i hiljada različitih signala i poruka. Elektronske komponente medusobno komuniciraju putem mreža zasnovanih na protokolima kao što su CAN, FlexRay ili LIN. U ovom radu je opisano rešenje koje bazirano na tri modula koja se mogu upotrebiti za pracenje rada odredjenih EKJ i ispitivanje korektnosti komunikacije izmedu istih.

articleTitle: Optimal source localization in a real radio channel
abstract: In this paper, TOA localization model is presented for passive source localization. Localization problem is formulated as an optimization problem with the sum of squared errors as the objective function. Gauss-Newton optimization method is applied in order to determine optimal transmitter location. We considered radio channel in the presence of Gaussian noise. Computer numerical simulation results in MATLAB are presented for linear and nonlinear TOA localization methods, as well as their mutual correlation.

articleTitle: Automated linked data generation from the transport administration domain
abstract: The Linked Data approach in data publishing allows the users and their data-driven applications to have broader use cases which encompass various data sources, either publicly available on the Web, or in private repositories. The use of W3C standards in publishing such data enables uniform access across platforms. Transport information today has higher importance to the citizens and society than ever and accessing the right information at the right time can improve the quality of everyday life for many people in the world. In this paper, we describe our approach of building a system for automated Linked Data generation from the transportation domain. We used the data from the Swedish Transport Administration (STA) as a specific case study. For the purpose of RDF annotation, we developed the Transport Administration Ontology (TAO). The resulting five-star data enables advanced use case scenarios over the original STA data, which we also demonstrate with our web application.

articleTitle: Verification of frequency analysis experimental setup
abstract: In a variety of engineering tasks, accurate measurement of signal spectrum presents necessary requirement. Hardware bring-up with noise sources tracing, through DC power sources validation and profiling, AD and DA signal conversion, communication channels verification, mutual units influence checks and many other applications lean on frequency analysis results. In many real life scenarios engineers take frequency spectrum results from the measurement units as is, without deeper investigation abut measurement uncertainty, especially related to ratio between signal period and windowing function length which could introduce significant differences. Aim of this paper is to highlight two things, first is advantage of automated custom tailored test setup, which decreases probability of gross errors and second is error validation of the harmonic content of complex periodical signals. Digital high-end oscilloscope with embedded FFT function including several windowing functions is used as test unit in automation process and also for the measurement error investigation.

articleTitle: Simplified analysis of orthogonal matching pursuit performance in compressed sensing
abstract: We perform theoretical analysis of compressed sensing with Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) recovery. In the analysis we utilize an OMP simplification where the estimation step in each iteration is assumed to be perfect. We consider the case when the noise is AWGN, the signal is sparse with equal energy nonzero components and the measurement matrix has i.i.d. Gaussian entries. We estimate the probability of perfect support reconstruction. We then extend the analysis to the Multiple Measurement Vector case. The analysis sheds new light on the compressed sensing recovery and gives a close estimate of the OMP reconstruction performance.

articleTitle: Optimization of non-blocking packet networks using load balanced shortest path routing
abstract: In this paper, we present the performance of the proposed two-phase routing protocol, which is based on load balancing and shortest path routing. We refer to this protocol as load balanced shortest path routing (LB-SPR). The proposed routing protocol can be optimized using linear programming, in order to maximize the network throughput, or minimize the cost of setting up the network that can support given traffic demands. The performance of LB-SPR is compared with the performance of the regular shortest path routing, and it is shown that the proposed routing strategy increases the network throughput and reduces network cost for real wide area network topologies.

articleTitle: Parameters estimation of random sequence in the stochastic calculating devices
abstract: In this article we introduce the concept of probabilistic binary element provides requirements, which ensure compliance with the criterion of "uniformity" in the implementation of the basic physical generators uniformly distributed random number sequences. Based on these studies, we obtained an analytic relation between the parameters of the binary sequence and parameters of a numerical sequence with the shift register output.

articleTitle: eWISENS — Simulation of the wireless sensor networks and graph algorithms
abstract: The basic features of a software system developed to support the teaching of Wireless sensor networks, and the experiences in using it for simulation of the graph algorithms have been presented in the paper. It allows users to design and simulate wireless sensor networks, represent them in the form of graph and perform various graph algorithms and spectral analysis. Simulators are very useful aid in teaching process, especially in the area of wireless sensor networks and graph theory. Simulation can help students to understand complex algorithms and topics through visualization of the difficult concepts.

articleTitle: Impact of HPA nonlinearity on downlink signal degradation in satellite communications
abstract: In this paper an impact of high power amplifier (HPA) nonlinearity on downlink signal constellation in satellite communications is analyzed. The variations in the signal envelope affecting the amplitude and phase of the output signal referred to as amplitude (AM-AM) and phase (AM-PM) envelope characteristics due to HPA nonlinearity, are computed according to the Saleh's model. Different values of HPA back-off level are used in simulation process, moving the HPA operating point from moderate to severe nonlinearity region. 16-QAM constellation format is proposed, while the input and output signal constellation is computed for different values of back-off level, showing phase rotation and amplitude compression in the output signal constellation.

articleTitle: An affine combination of adaptive filters for sparse impulse response identification
abstract: In this paper we present an affine combination strategy for two adaptive filters. One filter is designed to handle sparse impulse responses and the other one performs better if impulse response is dispersive. Filter outputs are combined using an adaptive mixing parameter and the resulting output shows better performance than each of the combining filters separately. We also demonstrate that affine combination results in faster convergence than convex combination of two adaptive filters.

articleTitle: Design of the new advanced modes for the mobile platform control application
abstract: In this paper, designing of the new advanced modes for the mobile platform control application is described. During the project it was first necessary to add new hardware modules to the mobile platform current concept and improve firmware of the several modules that were already mounted. After that the main goal of this project was to design the C# application with different possibilities of controlling the platform. It collects data from all the sensors and allows regulation of the movement in four modes. Joystick control mode was improved from the previous projects with obstacle detection. Glyph following mode was also improved to allow better movement possibilities. Finally two new modes were created: human figure recognition with following of the basic gestures and autonomous navigation with obstacle detection and avoiding.

articleTitle: Towards customers & service oriented mobile service providers
abstract: Moving from network-oriented towards customers & service - oriented operations is a step towards improving business KPIs. Customer Experience Management (CEM) is identified as a key differentiator for Mobile Service Providers to stay competitive in the market. CEM approach is designed to focus on procedures and a methodology to satisfy the service quality needs of each end-user. In this paper, we have analyzed current state in performance/customer management segment for MSPs in Bosnia and Herzegovina. We have presented a short overview of transformation journey from network-oriented to service-oriented solution with the Service Operation Center at the heart of a MSP's CEM strategy.

articleTitle: The development of phone duration model in speech synthesis in the Serbian language
abstract: Having in mind the importance of segmental duration from the perceptual point of view, the possibility of automatic prediction of natural duration of phones is essential for achieving the naturalness of synthetic speech. In this paper various machine learning techniques were used for phone duration modeling of the Serbian language. In this paper different phone duration models for the Serbian language using linear regression, tree-based algorithms and meta-learning algorithms such as additive regression, bagging and stacking algorithm are presented. Phone duration models have been developed for the full phoneme set of the Serbian language as well as for vowels and consonants separately. A large speech corpus and a feature set of 21 parameters describing phones and their contexts were used for segmental duration prediction. These features have been extracted from the large speech database for the Serbian language. The phone duration model obtained using additive regression method outperformed the other models developed for the Serbian language which are also presented in this paper. The results obtained for the full phoneme set as well as for consonants and vowels are comparable with or even outperform those reported in the literature for Czech, Greek, English, Lithuanian, Korean, Turkish and Indian languages Hindi and Telugu.

articleTitle: An analysis of hierarchical routing protocols for large WSN under the non-ideal connectivity conditions
abstract: The hierarchical routing protocols are often considered as energy-efficient solution for wireless sensor networks. Commonly observed single-hop and dual-hop hierarchical routing protocols do not support non-ideal connectivity conditions that cause degradation of performances, i.e. lower energy-efficiency and data delivery success. In this paper, LEACH, E-SEP and DECC protocols are analyzed for large WSNs under non-ideal connectivity conditions. Protocol modifications are suggested, which were shown, by Monte-Carlo experiments, to facilitate the performance improvement under the observed application conditions.

articleTitle: Web caching and content switching for performance of content delivery
abstract: With the emergence of web 2.0 the web has evolved from informational posting board to rich application platform. Web applications have replaced desktop applications from office productivity to 3d rendering. In this paper we'll present issues that degrade user web experience and increase demand for resource as well as techniques for mitigating those issues. We'll specially focus on large legacy web sites with legacy infrastructure. The example that we will work on is the main site of a large international organization.
